title: Spirit Collection
intro: The foundation of Blake and Boky's collaborative work. This collection explores the beauty within, opening up the figure and diving into the inner structure. The driving force behind this project was to expose the inner world of the figure, one that usually isn't seen. Drawing attention to what is usually hidden became a conduit for deeper introspection. Subsequently, the engineering behind this first desire to open the figure also tied into the second desire : allowing the sculpture to be both static and in movement. Every artwork in this collection is subject to the rule of physics whereby their structure allows them to "dance" and be alive in accordance to their environment.

"Transcending traditional techniques while staying true to the essence of figurative sculpture is at the core of the Spirits collection."

The figure must be explored fully in order to be understood

title: In Lucem
intro: This sculpture is a quiet reflection on our role in the degradation of our ecosystem and the challenges of the Anthropocene era. It resonates with the humanitarian crises and the shadows of war that cloud our world. Yet, it refuses to surrender to despair. The inversion challenges us to re-evaluate our approach, to question the status quo, and to consider a path toward healing.

The radiant light that emanates from the sculpture is not just symbolic; it's a promise—a promise that we possess the power to mend, to restore, and to flourish. It reminds us that even when our world seems to hang upside down, we have the ability to set it right and create a future where our dreams can indeed flourish.

In its minimalist elegance, this sculpture serves as a poignant call to awaken from our environmental apathy. It implores us to listen to the cries of a planet in peril, to acknowledge the urgency of the Anthropocene, and to take tangible steps to mitigate the destruction of our ecosystem.

title: Figurative Poetry
intro: Figurative Poetry embodies that feeling that simmers within the soul, comes to a boil and erupts into pieces like KABOOM. It is the introspection that develops with pieces like "Das Ich Und Das Esch" or "Loosing Myself in you"
Boky's first solo sculptural collection digs deep into her psyche and comments on women's suppression from cultural canons
